title: Heritage intern, concession booth and termite program direction
subtitle: Electric ice resurfacer, strategic plan update, reserve policy, parking by-law changes and stormwater master plan endorsement.
overview: Council approved a heritage intern contract funded from the Heritage Reserve Fund. Provincial changes mean listed heritage properties must be designated within two years or removed from the municipal register, so staff want to speed up designations this year {{vote:m4}}.

Council also approved a lease for an operator to reopen the Sportsplex concession booth, closed since 2020, with a requirement that staff report back if the contract ends {{vote:m5}}. It awarded the purchase of an electric ice resurfacer for $149,407.70 {{vote:m6}}. Staff were directed to talk with a pest control vendor about a new termite management approach, after negotiations with the earlier vendor failed {{vote:m7}}.

Council approved the updated 2023 to 2026 Strategic Plan {{vote:m8}} and a new Reserve and Reserve Fund Policy with transfers between reserves {{vote:m9}}. A parking by-law amendment, with an enforcement campaign expected to begin soon, was authorized {{vote:m2}}. Consent items included endorsing the Stormwater Management Master Plan {{vote:m1}}. The fire chief was also authorized to sign an annual training access agreement with the Grand River Conservation Authority {{vote:m3}}.

decisions.detail: Council authorized Heritage Reserve Fund money for a heritage intern contract position and related administrative costs to support more heritage designations.
Council authorized a lease with a local operator to run the Sportsplex concession booth, and directed staff to report back on next steps if the contract ends.
Council awarded an electric ice resurfacer purchase to Zamboni Company Ltd. for $149,407.70.
Council directed staff to enter discussions with Aetna Pest Control and allowed an optional survey of property owners identified in the 2020 study.
Council approved the updated 2023 to 2026 Strategic Plan as presented, including a new business development priority.
Council adopted the updated policy, approved the recommended reserve transfers as of December 31, 2023, and authorized a by-law to enact it.
Council authorized the Mayor and Clerk to execute a by-law amending the township's parking and stopping by-law.
As part of the consent agenda, Council endorsed the plan, directed publication of the study completion notice, and asked staff to bring its projects forward in budget deliberations.

debate: On the heritage intern, staff said the provincial changes remove protection for non-designated listed properties, and designation takes extensive research and notice. Councillors asked about tourism use and whether an unofficial list could be kept; staff said an inventory list could preserve the information.

On the concession booth, one councillor wanted assurance that one vendor would not hold the booth indefinitely. Staff said the contract includes optional additional years. Another councillor wanted the booth to stay viable with options beyond closing it, which led to the report-back wording.

On the strategic plan, some councillors questioned whether the word "support" implied financial commitment. Staff said support could be financial or non-financial. After discussion, council kept the wording as presented.

On the reserve policy, councillors asked whether parks and recreation needs, such as a possible indoor recreation facility, should have a dedicated reserve. Staff said to wait for the feasibility study and keep flexible general reserves. Staff also agreed to show progress toward funding targets in future reports.
On termites, one councillor was concerned about timing and whether the program could happen this season. Staff said that depends on vendor discussions and could not be promised.
